finding: Every observed divergence is a permutation: the two policies produce the identical multiset of outcomes over the divergent rows, and the match-kind multiset over every whole document is identical. What differs is only which of two exactly-tied split halves receives AMBIGUOUS and which receives NEW. Neither policy merges, so no history is rewritten either way.
question: what are the OTHER-class divergences between LEGACY and BLOCKED
residual: The arbitrary tie-break between exactly-equal candidates is a pre-existing property of the Hungarian assignment and is present in LEGACY too. It is a reproducibility caveat for split halves, not a defect introduced by BLOCKED.
